Rehabilitation, sponsored by the project, will cause these properties to be reassessed at a rehabilitated value. A drain on tax revenues, attributable to the tax base, will also occur as a result of the maintenance requirements of the new public areas. The additional walkway and parking area lighting will also be maintained with City property tax revenues.
c. Public Debt
Since Federal funds will be used in combination with State funds to finance 100 percent of the project's activities, the public debt for the local jurisdiction will not be increased.
d. Health and Safety
The Health and Safety of the project residents, and the community in general, will be improved as a result of the rehabilitation and code enforcement activities. The redistribution of population, clearance of certain areas, and use of the proposed flood plain ordinance will help to protect residents in the event of future flooding.
The negative factors associated with the type of renewal activities scheduled for the project occur mainly in the execution stages of the project and are short term in nature. Reference is made to "Noise Levels" and "Atmosphere" above.
e. Neighborhood Viability
The neighborhood viability of the project area is an overall objective of the urban renewal plan and many of the scheduled project activities are designed to accomplish this objective. The positive impacts realized from open-spaces, new streets and sidewalks, trees, new zoning and land use, new residential buildings and new business, rehabilitation activities, code enforcement and project area lighting, all relate to the ultimate planned viability of the area. The adverse or negative impacts realized during, or at some point in, the execution stage, must be weighed against the final result. Negative impacts from construction activity and relocation activity tend to be overshadowed by the positive results over the long run. None of the negative items are considered to be of such a drastic nature that consideration should be given to their elimination from the plan. In many cases the negative aspects will be of short duration and will have no lasting adverse social, economic, or physical consequence once they have been completed or after sufficient time has elapsed to permit full realization of the regeneration process brought about by the renewal actions.
